entry.title: feat(client): the free build's trial gate quotes the live plan
entry.content:
feat(client): the free build's trial gate quotes the live plan

readsotto.app has no CloudAdapter, so its Discuss gate could not ask what a
subscription costs and hard-coded the answer: "3 days", "$9.99 a month or
$79 a year", written out in nine catalogs. A price change was a copy edit in
nine files that someone would forget.

The paid service already answers `GET /billing/plans` to anyone, no auth, off
the same plan table Stripe charges against. The gate now reads it:

- src/cloud/trialOffer.ts — `pickTrialOffer` (pure: first plan priced above
  zero, the same rule the paywall's card uses; `trialDays` or 3),
  `FALLBACK_TRIAL_OFFER` as the client's one remaining hard-coded price, and
  `useTrialOffer()`, which fetches once per app session (credentials omitted,
  4 s abort) and returns the fallback until the live values land. Offline, a
  500, a body that isn't a plans response, or a slow request all resolve to
  the fallback — silently, with no console noise on a stranger's first screen.
- src/cloud/priceFormat.ts — the paywall's `Intl.NumberFormat` lifted out so
  both screens format a price in one place. `formatUsd` is the paywall's,
  byte-identical to before (always cents). `formatUsdCompact` is for prose,
  where "$79.00 a year" reads like a form field.

Nothing else on the voice screen changes, and the paywall keeps reading
`cloud.plans()` exactly as it did.

entry.title: merge: security hardening onto the run 9 line (final main candidate)
entry.content:
merge: security hardening onto the run 9 line (final main candidate)

Merges `merge/security` (0453827 — the 2026-09-07 audit fixes on top of main
b2b65fc) into `merge/run9` (c6eb248 — run 9's Discuss-tutor work on top of the
same main). Merge base b2b65fc, so the security side of this merge is exactly
`security/hardening-2026-09-07`. Git reported two conflicts; both are in
packages/core.

packages/core/src/prompt.ts
  Both sides edited `buildSystemInstruction`'s tail. The security branch
  (fde8a89) fenced the session-context block where it still lived — inline in
  that function — wrapping the passage in `=== BOOK TEXT ===` /
  `=== END BOOK TEXT ===` and running `fenceSafe` over the book title, chapter
  title, sentence text, word text, saved words and turn summary. run 9 lane B
  had already lifted that same block out into `renderDynamicContext()` so the
  compact prompt for the in-browser 2B model could reuse it, and the tail was
  reduced to a call.

  Resolved by moving the security branch's fencing into
  `renderDynamicContext()`, not by taking either tail. Consequence: the fence
  and both neutralisations now apply to BOTH prompts. Proven, not asserted —
  a scratch suite built all four modes from this file and from each parent's:
  the non-compact output is byte-identical to merge/security's for every mode,
  and the compact output differs from merge/run9's only by the fence.

  The compact prompt's eleven numbered rules are byte-identical to
  merge/run9's in every mode: order, count, the reply contract, rule 6's
  `[[reading:]]` allowance and rule 3's current wording are all untouched.
  The one sentence added to compact is the security branch's own fence line,
  verbatim, appended to the head above the session context — the same position
  it holds in the full prompt. Without it the compact prompt would carry fence
  markers with nothing saying what they are, and fde8a89's `[[reading:]]`
  forgery finding is reachable precisely on that path (imported EPUB ->
  browser tutor -> markers.ts).

packages/core/src/prompt.test.ts
  Both sides appended a describe block at EOF. Kept both, in order: run 9
  lane B's compact suite and GOLDEN_NON_COMPACT fixture, then the security
  branch's "untrusted passage text is fenced as data" suite. The security
  branch's raise of the prompt-length ceiling (4600 -> 4800, for the fence)
  auto-merged and is kept.

  GOLDEN_NON_COMPACT had to be regenerated: the fence changes the non-compact
  bytes it pins, which is exactly the deliberate prompt change its docstring
  says to regenerate for. Four lines added per mode and nothing else — the
  two-line fence rule after "...wait through natural pauses.", and the
  `=== BOOK TEXT ===` / `=== END BOOK TEXT ===` markers around the sentence
  lines. Recorded in the docstring with the commit that caused it.

No security fencing test and no run 9 golden test had to be traded off:
packages/core/src/prompt.test.ts is 44/44.

(merge/run9 1062 + the security branch's 14); `npx vitest run packages/core`
81/81; `npx vitest run apps/server` 111/111; `pnpm lint` 0 errors / 27
pre-existing warnings; prettier clean on both resolved files;
`pnpm content:validate` 0 errors / 223 pre-existing warnings; `web:export`
exit 0; `BASE_URL=http://localhost:8092 node e2e/hosted.mjs` RESULT PASS with

entry.title: merge: main (origin PRs #1-#5 and run 10) into the run 9 line
entry.content:
merge: main (origin PRs #1-#5 and run 10) into the run 9 line

`main` moved to b2b65fc while merge/run9 was in flight — origin/main's PRs
#1-#5 (UX findings, capture gate by explicit mute and push-to-talk intent,
service-worker refresh per build, awaited streamed speech handlers, imported
narration, parchment covers) merged onto run 10. Two textual conflicts, both
in packages/voice/src/browser-cascade, plus one semantic conflict git could
not see, in packages/core/src/prompt. Nothing was taken wholesale.

1. protocol.ts, MainToWorker union. Both sides appended a member next to
   `ptt`: main's `turn_detection`, run 9's documented `playback_drained`.
   Kept both, main's first. `WorkerInitPayload`'s new `turnDetection`/`muted`
   auto-merged.

2. worker.ts, three hunks.
   - SessionState: kept main's `inputGeneration` epoch and run 9's
     `speaking` flag; the epoch gets the doc comment it never had.
   - transcribeSegment head: main's `session.muted` bail and the
     `s`/`generation`/`current()` epoch capture FIRST, then run 9's
     `measureSegment` stats. A segment that arrives after the learner muted
     is not measured, let alone transcribed. main's three `if (!current())
     return;` guards and `loadStt(s.payload.stt, 'wasm')` auto-merged and
     were checked, as did run 9's transcript gate and its `too_short` drop.
   - init: main's `muted: msg.payload.muted ?? false`, `inputGeneration: 0`
     and `turnMode: msg.payload.turnDetection ?? 'auto'` plus run 9's
     `speaking: false`.

   The `ptt` case auto-merged into exactly the wanted shape and was kept:
   main's `if (session && !session.muted)` guard and `turn_detection` case
   around run 9's `buffer.start(PTT_PRE_ROLL_MS)` and `too_short` drop. The
   pre-roll keeps its missing `clear()` because the capture gate's first
   case applies — the buffer cannot hold audio recorded while muted.
   `handleFrame` returns early on `session.muted` (worker.ts:1009-1010), the
   provider disables capture whenever muted (provider.ts `syncCapture`),
   `CaptureGate` drops callbacks while disabled, and the `mute` case clears
   the buffer on the way in. The first press after unmuting therefore has an
   empty pre-roll rather than a replay of the muted period. Recorded in a
   comment at the call site.

3. prompt.ts / prompt.test.ts (no conflict markers; the test suite found
   it). 3669ff5 deliberately rewrote the non-compact prompt's
   response-language sentence, and run 9's GOLDEN_NON_COMPACT fixture pins
   those bytes for all four modes. Regenerated the fixture — the guard did
   its job by failing on a deliberate change, which is what its docstring
   asks for — and carried the same priority into compact rule 3, so the
   in-browser tutor, the only caller of the compact prompt, keeps 3669ff5's
   behaviour instead of silently reverting it.

Both sides' streamed-speech contracts survive unchanged: ff9560e's awaited
`onTextDelta` on the server (llm.ts) auto-merged, run 9 having made no
server change, and the browser worker's own `await handlers.onTextDelta`
still sits inside cd326af's draining loop, so run 9's sentence cap aborts
through `interruptGenerate()` and the `finally` awaits it before `chat()`
resolves — the cap does not skip the await and the await does not resurrect
the WebLLM lock leak.

Proof: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 105 files / 1062 tests, all green
(merge/run9 alone 1046, main alone 856); @sotto/voice 18 files / 299 tests;
@sotto/client 48 files / 459 tests; eslint 0 errors tree-wide; prettier
clean on the resolved files; content:validate 0 errors / 223 warnings;
hosted smoke RESULT PASS with TAPS landing -> reader = 4 at 375 and 1440.
